newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares start firm at National Stock Exchange.
newsitem.headline: India shares start firm at National Stock Exchange.

text.p: Bombay stocks were quoted higher in mid-morning trade at the National Stock Exchange on Monday with trading yet to start at the Bombay bourse due to a power crisis, traders said.
Market activity was however limited to select stocks in the absence of trading done by local and foreign institutions, they said.
"Everyone is waiting for the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) to start trading," said Sanjeev Choithani, chief dealer at brokers Pashupati Advani.
"In the absence of any trend shown by the BSE, the market is purely in a speculative grip."
India's Housing Development & Finance Corporation (HDFC) shares were placed under a price limit after jumping 221.05 rupees, or nearly six percent, at 3,966.05 at the NSE.

Traders said foreign funds turned buyers in the stock after the firm on Friday said it had received central bank approval for foreign institutional investors (FIIs) to raise their holding limits to 30 percent from 24 percent.
Disbursals made by India's leading housing finance company rose 24 percent in the first few months of the current financial year, company officials said last week.
HDFC shares ended at 3,711.75 rupees at the BSE on Friday.
Stocks will kick off at the BSE close to 12-month highs after a five-week rise, and could drift higher at the start of its weekly account, traders said.
Bombay's index has rocketed nearly 34 percent so far this year, making it the best first-half gain in the last five years.

The blue chip gauge has shown a handsome gain of 427 points, or nearly 12 percent in the last five weeks, closing at 4,133.24, on Friday just short of the 52-week high of 4,153.80 scaled earlier in the day.
The BSE will get off to a delayed start on Monday due to a power crisis at the bourse.
A BSE statement to its members did not give any time for the delayed opening.
